claims.text: The initial Mg-containing lightweight HEA is a homogeneous, metastable, non-equilibrium solid solution with Mg and the other principal elements uniformly distributed.
Thermal activation during service induces chemical short-range ordering in the alloy.
Thermally induced short-range ordering locally enriches Mg.
Local Mg enrichment triggers precipitation of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds, primarily at grain boundaries.
Mg-rich intermetallic phases nucleate and grow once a critical local Mg concentration is reached.
Intermetallic precipitates modify the alloy's ability to form a continuous protective high-temperature oxide scale.
Intermetallic precipitates alter local electrochemical properties.
Finely dispersed, coherent Mg-rich precipitates may nucleate a protective oxide layer and sustain oxidation resistance.
Small, uniformly dispersed precipitates may permit retention of corrosion resistance.
Coarsened or discontinuous intermetallics can act as local galvanic sites.
Coarsened or uneven intermetallic distributions disrupt protective-film continuity.
Coarse or uneven intermetallic distributions produce a measurable decrease in corrosion resistance relative to the initial state.
Thermally aged samples will develop Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates at grain boundaries relative to the as-solid-solution state.
The initial metastable solid solution has excellent corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The initial state's resistance results from uniform elemental distribution and the absence of detrimental intermetallic phases.
The kinetics of short-range-order formation and intermetallic precipitation depend on aging temperature and duration.
Insufficient aging will fail to trigger significant microstructural changes, whereas excessive coarsening may degrade protective properties.
The proposed service regime includes temperatures above 500 degrees Celsius and chloride-containing media such as 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
A lack of statistically significant precipitation after aging, together with unchanged or uniformly improved corrosion and oxidation resistance, would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis frames precipitation as leading to either enhanced or degraded resistance, whereas the predicted outcome frames the favorable branch as retention rather than enhancement.
